title: Queue visibility and human override surface for agent orchestration
body:
Part of: #165
Depends on: #239, #240, #241

## Summary
The orchestrator is only useful if a human can understand and steer it.

We need a GitHub-native queue and override surface so maintainers can see what is pending/running/blocked, understand why a finding was routed a certain way, and intervene without digging through raw Actions logs or local artifacts.

## Red
- Queue state is fragmented across local artifacts, workflow logs, and issue comments.
- There is no single operator surface for `hold`, `retry`, `approve`, `route-to-human`, or `force-manual` decisions.
- It is not yet easy to hand the same queued item to a human using Codex/Claude interactively with their personal subscriptions.

## Green
A maintainer can open GitHub and answer:
- what is queued
- what is running
- what is blocked
- why each item was routed that way
- what human action, if any, is needed next

And they can intervene from GitHub without editing repo code.

## Scope
- Define a GitHub-native queue visibility surface:
  - Project view, issue/PR comment digest, and/or generated dispatch ledger summaries
- Expose per-item state such as:
  - finding/issue ref
  - current route
  - owner/executor
  - latest PR/issue link
  - last validation result
  - next action needed
- Add operator controls via trusted comments and/or workflow dispatch inputs:
  - hold
  - retry
  - approve
  - reject
  - route to human
  - force manual Codex/Claude handoff
- Generate manual task prompts so a maintainer can use personal Codex/Claude subscriptions interactively against the same queued item
- Persist human feedback/override state so later orchestration passes do not forget it
- Make final human approval state explicit before merge/prod promotion

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A maintainer can view pending/in-progress/blocked/completed agent work from GitHub without opening raw run artifacts
- [ ] Each routed item exposes its route reason, current links, and next action
- [ ] A maintainer can hold/retry/approve/reject from GitHub using trusted controls
- [ ] Manual Codex/Claude task prompts are generated from the same queue item for interactive use
- [ ] Human feedback/override state persists and is visible to later orchestration passes
- [ ] The queue separates unattended-safe work from work waiting on human judgment or approval

## Suggested Lane
`qa-platform`

## Human Gate
Required
